mio: mio — my (unstressed possessive; mio Çid 'my lord Cid')
çid: Çid — the Cid, 'lord' (Arabic sīdī 'my lord'; pronounced Tsid)
ganançia: ganançia — gain, profit, interest (= ganancia) · also booty, spoils of war (de ganançia 'as booty'; feremos grand ganançia 'we shall take great spoils')
en: en — in, into, on · en — of it, thence (= ende; por en avemos qué fablar 'of which we have to speak') · also en — 'as' (en paria 'as tribute'); en essora 'at that moment'
alcoçer: Alcoçer — Alcocer, a Moorish town the Cid camps before; site now unknown (Pidal: on the left of the Jalón, between Ateca and Calatayud)
fizo: fazer — he made, did, caused (strong preterite 3rd sg.; fizo posar 'he made (them) halt'; = hizo)
por: por — through, along, by, for · purpose, 'in order to' (por el reyno quitar 'to quit the kingdom'); por + inf. 'yet to be done' (tres an por troçir 'three remain to pass'); 'for, on behalf of' (por mio Çid) · also por — 'out of, because of' (por miedo 'through fear'); 'for (that reason)' (por tal lo faze 'he does it for that reason'); 'by way of' (por Guadalfajara); por + noun 'for the sake of' ; por coraçón 'willingly' · also 'for (a price)' (por quanto serié conprada 'for how much it would be bought'); 'by means of' (por carta 'by writ'); 'through, thanks to' (por mí ganaredes 'through me you will gain') · also por — 'on, during (a time)' (por aquesta mañana 'this morning'); 'by way of, through' (por medio de la llaña 'through the middle of the plain')
que: que — that, who, which; for · also por que — because, since (= porque) · por que — by which, whereby (por que más valdrá 'whereby he will be worth more') · also que — 'so that, lest' introducing purpose/result (que por miedo non dexen nada; por tal lo faze … que no lo ventasse nadi); after después/mientra 'after, while' (después que, mientra que)
a: a — to, at · also aver — he/she has (3rd sg. present, h-less spelling of ha, as in el rey me a ayrado = el rey me ha airado) · personal a before a direct object (salvest a Jonás; a ti adoro); a + inf. 'to, about to' (tornólas a catar); a tan grand sabor 'with so great pleasure'; a ojo 'in plain sight' · also a — 'into' (sacar a çelada 'to lure into ambush'); 'at, in' (a la çaga 'at the rear'); 'against' (dar salto a la çaga); dative 'to' (a mí dedes); haber a + inf. 'have to' (lo han a far); a + noun of direction (adeliñava a la puerta 'made for the gate') · impersonal 'there is' (aver; es dia a de plazo 'there is (only) a day of the term', the most likely reading of a hard line); ha as auxiliary set after the participle (soñado a 'he has dreamt') · also 'on, at (a time)' (a tercer dia 'on the third day')
los: el — the (masc. pl.); them (object pronoun) · also los que 'those who' (demonstrative use before a relative); los — him, them as object of consejar (commo los consejava 'as he advised them') · also los de 'those of' (con los de Castejón 'with the men of Castejón')
de: de — of, from · also de — by (the agent with a passive participle; = por) · also de — 'by (night)' (de noch), partitive 'of, among' (quinze moros … de los que alcançava; pocas de gentes), 'as' (de ganançia 'as booty'), 'from outside' (de fuera), 'on the right' (de diestro) · also 'about, concerning' (de mí non digan mal 'let them not speak ill of me') · also de — 'as if in' (commo de arrancada 'as if in rout'); 'in the manner of' (de guisa 'in such a way'); 'of, among' (de bivos pocos 'of the living few'); nominalized infinitive (del prender 'of the taking')
teca: Teca — Ateca, place in Zaragoza province (traditional identification)
e: e — and (= modern y) · also aver — I have (1st sg. present, apocopated form of he, perfect auxiliary: Espeso e el oro, 'I have spent the gold')
terrer: Terrer — place name, a town near Calatayud (probably modern Terrer, Zaragoza province)
sabet: saber — know, mark you (imperative 2nd pl., sabed; sabet = sabed; epic tag addressed to the audience)
va: ir — he/she goes (present 3rd sg.; = va); ir + gerund, 'to be (gradually) doing' · ir + infinitive 'goes to' (la manol va besar 'goes to kiss his hand', el Duero va passar 'goes to cross the Duero')
al: a + el — to the; al menos 'even the least' · also a + el standing for a + la before a feminine noun beginning with a vowel (al espada = a la espada) · also al — 'other thing, the rest' (neuter, Latin alius; de lo al non pienssan nada 'of anything else they think nothing'; distinct from a + el)
uno: uno — one; en uno = 'together, as one' · el uno ... el otro 'the one ... the other' (el uno es en paradiso, ca el otro non entró)
roy: Roy — Ruy, short for Rodrigo (Roy Díaz = Rodrigo Díaz, the Cid)
bivar: Bivar — Vivar, the Cid's home village just north of Burgos
alfonsso: Alfonsso — Alfonso (VI, king of León and Castile)
tierra: tierra — land, country; one's own land · earth (fezist çielo e tierra 'you made heaven and earth'; por tierra 'on earth')
echado: echar — cast out, exiled (past part.; = echado)
lo: lo — him, it (object pronoun) · lo que perdedes 'that which you lose' (neuter antecedent of the relative) · also lo — neuter article 'what is' (lo to 'what is yours'); pleonastic 'it' (lo an, lo han a far; por tal lo faze 'for that reason he does it')
ha: aver — he has (3rd sg. present; = ha) · ha — to (a with h-, aver a + inf. 'will, must': lo an todos ha far 'all are to do it'); aver — has, possesses (las fijas que ha 'the daughters she has') · also ha — future ending after infinitive + clitics, the split future (tornar nos la ha 'he will give it back to us'; = nos la tornará)
vino: vino — wine (noun); also venir — he came (strong preterite 3rd sg.; por en vino a aquesto, 'that is how he came to this pass')
posar: posar — to lodge, halt for the night (infinitive; = posar)
sobre: sobre — upon, over; here 'on the security of' (sobre aquellas arcas) · sobre Navas de Palos 'above, hard by Navas de Palos' (position along the route) · also 'before, against (a town to be besieged)' (sobre Alcoçer iva posar 'went to camp before Alcocer')
un: uno — a, one (apocopated masc. before a noun)
çelada: çelada — ambush (en çelada 'in ambush'; sacar a çelada 'to draw out into an ambush'; = celada, 'ambush, trap')
el: el — the (masc.) · also el — 'he who' before a relative (el qui quisiere, el que es sobre Fenares); el before a fem. noun beginning with a vowel (el espada = la espada; el algara = la algara)
castiello: castiello — castle (= castillo; here the castle quarter of Burgos) · also the castle of Castejón (el castiello dexó en so poder)
si: si — if; si + subjunctive alone = 'if only …!'
salón: Salón — the river Jalón (the old form of the name; = Jalón)
mal: mal — harm, hurt, ruin · mal — evil, in the prayer's sense (por end es salvo de mal 'therefore he is saved from evil')
es: seer — it is (present 3rd sg.) · also ser as perfect auxiliary of intransitives (exido es 'has gone out') and passive auxiliary (la tienda es cogida)
le: le — to him, him (dative pronoun) · also le — him, as direct object (leísmo; si ellos le prenden 'if they take him'); dative (non se le dava 'did not surrender to him')
moros: moro — Moor (masc. pl.); a moros nin a cristianos, 'to any living soul' (merism)
id: ir — go! (2nd pl. imperative; id vos 'go (you)', with reflexive vos; = id, idos)
lidiar: lidiar — to fight (infinitive; = lidiar, closest luchar)
vos: vos — you (object pronoun, polite/plural) · also subject 'you' (vos, que por mí dexades 'you who leave for my sake'); dative 'to you' (dar vos quiero vuestra part) · also reflexive/ethic 'you (yourselves)' (id vos en algara 'go off on a raid'); dative with an impersonal sense (si cueta vos fore 'if need befall you')
delant: delant — ahead, in front (apocopated adverb; = delante)
me: me — me, to me · also reflexive 'myself' (fata que yo me pague 'until I am satisfied')
dar: dar — to give (infinitive; split future dar gelos [hemos] = se los daremos) · also dar salto 'to make a dash, sally' (salto davan); dar çevada 'to give barley, feed the horses'
cavalgan: cavalgar — they ride, mount (present 3rd pl.; = cabalgan)
pienssan: pensar — they think; pensar de + inf. 'to set about (doing)' (epic formula)
andar: andar — to travel, go on (infinitive; = andar)
ellos: ellos — they, them (stressed 3rd pl. masc. pronoun)
noch: noche — night (apocopated form of noche; cf. anoch)
otro: otro — other, another (masc.; el otro 'the other'; = otro) · also otro día 'the next day'; lo otro 'the rest'
mañana: mañana — morning (a la mañana 'in the morning'; otro dia mañana 'next morning'; = mañana)
partes: parte — part, quarter, direction (pl.); de todas partes 'from every quarter'
ixieron: exir — they went out (preterite 3rd pl.; = salieron)
dizen: dezir — they say, they call (present 3rd pl.; do dizen monte Calvarie 'where they call (it) Mount Calvary'; = dicen)
andidieron: andar — they travelled, marched (strong preterite 3rd pl.; = anduvieron)
todo: todo — all, every (de todo conducho, 'with every kind of provision')
l: le — to him (elided before vowel: l'an = le han)
vagar: vagar — leisure, slowness (noun; de vagar 'at leisure, unhurriedly'; = vagar, closest despacio)
dan: dar — they give (present 3rd pl.; vagar non se dan 'they allow themselves no leisure'; = dan) · also dar — 'to pay (tribute)' (dan parias 'they pay tribute')
pregones: pregón — public proclamation, crier's announcement (pl.; = pregones)
bueno: bueno — good, fine, great (qué bueno es el gozo 'how great is the joy'; = bueno)
van: ir — they go (present 3rd pl.) · also ir + gerund 'keep going' (passando van 'they go on passing')
las: el/la — the (fem. pl.); them (fem. object pronoun)
ca: ca — for, because (Latin quia) · ca — perhaps 'but, whereas' (el uno es en paradiso, ca el otro non entró allá; the sense is uncertain)
yentes: yente — people, folk (= gente; y- from Latin g-)
son: seer — they are (3rd pl.) · also son — perfect auxiliary of intransitives and passive auxiliary (todos son exidos 'have all gone out'; nombrados son; son derramadas 'are scattered')
andan: andar — they go about, range (present 3rd pl.; = andan)
ya: ya — O! (vocative particle, Arabic yā); also 'now, already' · also ya — 'would', reduced imperfect of aver as conditional ending, 3rd sg., after infinitive + clitic (pagar se ya 'would be satisfied'; = -ía)
mesnadas: mesnada — household troop, band of followers (pl.; = mesnadas)
exir: exir — to go out, leave (infinitive; = salir)
querién: querer — they wished, would (imperfect 3rd pl.; = querían)
ora: hora — hour (= hora); en buen ora, part of the poem's honorific birth-formula, 'born in a good hour' · al ora 'at that very hour, then' (en ti crovo al ora)
nasco: nacer — he was born (strong preterite 3rd sg.; = nació)
firme: firme — firm; used adverbially, 'firmly, securely' (= firmemente)
gelo: ge + lo — it to him/them (ge, ancestor of modern se, + lo; = se lo)
çerca: çerca — near; here adverbial, çerca o tarde = 'sooner or later' (= cerca)
complidas: complido — complete, full (fem. pl.; complidas quinze sedmanas 'a full fifteen weeks'; = cumplidas)
cabo: cabo — beside, next to (preposition; cf. modern cabe) · also cabo — end (noun; fasta cabo del año, 'until the end of the year')
entrar: entrar — to enter, set in (infinitive; = entrar)
sos: so — his, her, their (= modern sus)
tornós: tornar + se — she turned back (tornó + -s(e): after a stressed vowel -se shrinks to -s) · also tornarse a + inf. 'to set to, begin' (tornós a sonrisar 'he broke into a smile', perhaps 'smiled again'; the Cid the subject)
nos: nos — we (subject pronoun; = nosotros) · also nos — us, to us (object pronoun; atorgar nos hedes 'you will grant us') · also reflexive 'ourselves' (nos partimos 'we part'); dative (la missa nos dirá 'will say for us')
an: aver — they have (3rd pl. present of aver = han) · perfect auxiliary (passados los an 'they have passed'; la missa acabada la an 'they have finished'); an por troçir 'there remain to pass'; an ... ha far 'they have to do, are to do'
no: no — not (variant spelling of non) · also nos — to us (nos elided before lo: no' lo, 'to us it')
far: far — to do (apocopated infinitive of fazer; = hacer)
fabló: fablar — he spoke (preterite; = habló, note f-)
minaya: Minaya — the title by which the Cid's kinsman Álvar Fáñez is called, usually explained as mi + anaya 'my brother'
exidos: exir — gone out (past part. masc. pl.; son exidos 'have gone out', ser as auxiliary; = salidos)
somos: seer — we are (1st pl. of seer = ser)
darán: dar — they will give (future 3rd pl.; = darán)
bien: bien — well · bien — good, benefit (noun; algún bien vos pueda far 'some good I may do you') · bien — very, quite, intensifying an adverb (bien çerca del agua 'very near the water')
más: más — more; e más 'and moreover' · non más 'no more, nothing more'; por que más valdrá 'whereby he will be worth more'
nombre: nombre — name; por nombre 'by name, called' (= nombre)
cras: cras — tomorrow (adverb, Latin cras; cras a la mañana 'tomorrow morning'; modern uses mañana)
dixo: dezir — he/she said (strong preterite; x = sh-sound; = dijo)
campeador: Campeador — the Battler, the Champion (the Cid's epithet, from campo 'field of battle')
guisa: guisa — manner, fashion; a guisa de 'in the fashion of'
aver: aver — wealth, property, goods (noun use of aver, beside aver the verb 'to have')
fuera: fuera — outside, out of doors (adverb; de fuera 'outside, from outside'; = fuera)
sopiesse: saber — he should know (imperfect subjunctive of saber; = supiese)
poridad: poridad — secrecy, privacy, confidence (= puridad); en poridad 'in confidence'
quantos: quanto — as many as (masc. pl.; todos quantos 'all who'; = cuantos)
él: él — he (stressed subject pronoun) · also él — 'him, it' after a preposition, of a thing (a él vino; en él fincaredes 'in it', i.e. in Castejón)
fablava: fablar — he was speaking (imperfect 3rd sg.; = hablaba)
commo: commo — as, like (spelling variant of como) · how, that, in the way that (commo sirva a doña Ximena 'how he is to serve doña Ximena'); like (commo la uña de la carne) · also commo si + imperfect subjunctive — 'as if' (commo si escapasse 'as if he were fleeing')
odredes: oír — you will hear (future 2nd pl., old -edes ending; = oiréis; the minstrel's aside to his listeners)
sinon: sinon — if not, otherwise, but rather (= sino, si no)
campo: campo — field, open ground, field of battle (= campo; en el campo 'in the open field'; the element in Campeador) · campo de Taranz 'the plain of Taranz'
per: Per — Pero, short for Pedro (Per Vermudoz = Pedro Bermúdez, a vassal of the Cid)
seña: seña — banner, standard (= seña; modern seña is 'sign', the banner sense is enseña)
sodes: seer — you are (2nd pl. present, used respectfully to one person; = sois; old -edes ending, cf. odredes, vedes, catedes)
sin: sin — without · also sin — 'besides, apart from' (sin las peonadas 'besides the foot-soldiers'); sin falla 'without fail'; sin dubda
mas: mas — but · also mas — 'most' (superlative, = más; en todo lo mas alto 'on the very highest part')
ella: ella — she, her (stressed 3rd sg. fem. pronoun)
mano: mano — hand (sg.); en vuestra mano = 'in your keeping'
tomar: tomar — to take (infinitive) · to seize, catch (en su tierra le pudies tomar 'could seize him in his land')
salto: salto — leap, jump · also dash, sally (dar salto 'to make a sortie'; non osa ninguno dar salto a la çaga 'none dares to dash at the rearguard')
tornar: tornar — to return; tornar palabra 'to answer a word' · also tornar — 'to give back' (tornar nos la ha doblada 'will give it back to us doubled'; infinitive + enclitic + ha, future); to turn (round), transitive (mandó tornar la seña 'he had the banner turned about')
qué: qué — what a …! (exclamative) · also qué — what? which? (interrogative pronoun/adjective, as in de qué será pagado, 'with what will he be satisfied') · indirect: que non sabe qué se far '(so that) she knows not what to do'; avemos qué fablar 'we have something to speak of'
priessa: priessa — haste, bustle (a una priessa 'all in one bustle'; = prisa) · also a priessa — 'quickly, in haste' (adverbial; a priessa espoloneavan 'they spurred in haste')
querié: querer — it was about to (imperfect 3rd sg., -ié ending; la noch querié entrar 'night was about to fall'; = quería) · also querer — he wished (imperfect 3rd sg.; commo querié trasnochar 'how he wished to travel by night'; = quería)
veriedes: veer — you would have seen (conditional 2nd pl.; = veríais; the minstrel's aside to the audience)
señas: señas — one each, one apiece (distributive adjective, fem. pl., Latin singulas; = sendas)
pendones: pendón — pennon, lance-banner (men are counted by lances)
qui: qui — he who, whoever (old relative pronoun, Latin qui; = quien)
manos: mano — hand (pl.); dar las manos = the handclasp that makes an agreement binding
fata: fata — until, as far as (variant of fasta; = hasta)
vala: valer — may he avail, protect (present subjunctive; vos vala 'may he keep you')
debdo: debdo — debt, obligation (= deuda); aver en debdo 'to be bound by a vow'
avedes: aver — you have (2nd pl. present, -edes; perfect auxiliary with a participle, me avedes mandado 'you have granted me'; = habéis)
veré: veer — I shall see (future 1st sg.; = veré)
sea: seer — may be, that is (present subjunctive 3rd sg.)
respuso: responder — he answered (strong preterite 3rd sg.; = respondió)
ganar: ganar — to gain, earn · also 'to capture, take (a fortress)' (Alcoçer cueda ganar 'he expects to take Alcocer') · also ganar — to till, work the land (Pidal, like Old French gaignier; non se treven ganar 'they dare not work their fields'; = labrar)
